items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: Okay, this is the most impressive thing I've seen in a long time. That's a spaceship that's about as tall as a 15story building coming back from space. And this tower just caught it out of the air with two giant arms. It's SpaceX's Starship and this is footage from Texas on Saturday. It's the first spaceship ever caught coming back from orbit and they did it on their first try. It circled the Earth 14 times at over 17,000 mph. It then belly flopped through the atmosphere to slow down. Then lights three engines, flips upright, and then slides sideways into those arms. So, you know, kind of like parallel parking a building. Pretty much every other rocket launch has thrown this part away afterwards, which is just insane because now that they know how to catch it, they could refuel it over and over again and fly it like an airplane. Now, the booster, which is the half that we've seen it catch before, actually ran low on fuel and blew up over the Gulf during the initial launch. But catching the actual spaceship was the thing they were going for. And this ship was number 42 with the words, "Don't panic," written on the side, which the booster portion clearly couldn't read. But this is one of the most amazing feats in modern space travel. So share this with a friend who loves rockets and future technology and make sure to follow for all the latest coolest tech and AI

items.transcript: This might be the coolest thing you're going to see today. This giant robot 3D prints buildings out of concrete. And right now, it's printing one in San Antonio for a company that sells bulldozers and excavators. It's called Vulcan and it's from Austin, Texas. And they've already printed over 270 buildings. It's about 46 ft wide and it works kind of like a soft serve ice cream machine, squeezing out a line of concrete and then stacking it in layers. So, that makes it so the walls could curve however they want. And Icon says that walls that used to take 30 to 45 days can now be done in 7 to 10 days. And they want these ones done by Thanksgiving. And if you've ever hired a contractor before, that's probably like the least believable part of what we're seeing here. Now, it's not printing the whole building, just like the offices and the training rooms. The big showroom for all the machines is actually still made out of steel. But there's a bigger picture here. NASA gave Icon $57 million to figure out how to print on the moon using moon dust. And I think that's pretty cool.

items.transcript: This might be the coolest thing you see today. This guy built a self-driving car that rolls on four giant balls. So, it can actually like drive sideways. And he actually rides it with his hands in the air, which, you know, also takes some balls. His name is James Bruton, and this is all real. He made those wheels out of plywood. And I love how this works because each ball is two halves of one axle. So, a motor rolls it one way and the halves spin freely the other way, kind of like an office chair. To drive itself, it's got two laser scanners and a $400 Arduino as the brain. So, he picks a spot on the map and then it weaves through these boxes all on its own. But then he put a mannequin in its path and it well, it drove right over it. And he figures the legs were just a little too skinny for the lasers to see. And it only goes about 1 mph. So, it was a very slow and run. And his fix was these two little fake trees next to him. So, share this with a friend who loves self-driving cars and cool gadgets and click that follow button to see the coolest tech and AI news every single day.
